messages:
dmitri (ml-runtime): quick PSA — ran the FP8+GPTQ bakeoff on Mistral-3 this morning, and the CUDA14 + Triton serving path shows a consistent 2.5x tail latency spike vs CUDA13. looks specific to the Triton/TRT-LLM flow, vLLM path is fine.

ben (infra): oof. any driver/kernel logs? did you try the same model on a clean container?

dmitri (ml-runtime): yep, repro on clean ubuntu:22.04 image with nvidia/cuda:14.0-runtime. stack: Triton 23.11 snapshot, TRT-LLM fork with our AWQ/GPTQ kernels. nvidia-smi shows driver 535.86. Maybe a kernel fallback causing syncs. snippet below: 

```
[2026-03-19T09:12:01Z] model_request: seq_len=1024 batch=1
[2026-03-19T09:12:01Z] using kernel: attention_fp8_fast_path
[2026-03-19T09:12:01Z] kernel fallthrough -> attention_generic_sync (slow)
[2026-03-19T09:12:03Z] latency p95=310ms (expected ~120ms)
```

carla (sre): interesting that it picks fp8_fast_path then falls back. could be cuBLAS/cuDNN ABI mismatch triggering non-fused kernels.

alice (ml-eng): does GPTQ vs AWQ differ? AWQ earlier looked more robust on this config, right?

eva (research): AWQ quant pipeline uses different reorder+packing, so its kernel selector picks a different launch config. i suspect the problem is memory allocator fragmentation + Triton executor behavior under CUDA14 — small extra syncs surface as big latency for large seq.

ben (infra): can you dump CUDA kernel list and driver symbols? also try forcing the fused kernel via env: `TRTLLM_FORCE_FUSED=1`.

dmitri (ml-runtime): tried that, forcing fused kernel avoids the fallthrough and latencies drop back to expected. but forcing is a workaround — we need to understand why selection fails. i attached the triton backend log (excerpt): 

```
triton: kernel_probe: attention_fp8_fast_path available=true
triton: runtime_link: cuBLAS ver=11.12, cuDNN ver=8.6
triton: symbol_lookup: cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx -> OK
triton: launcher: shader_compile success
triton: kernel_launch failed: cudaErrorLaunchTimeout -> fallback
```

carla (sre): cudaErrorLaunchTimeout on immediate kernel? that sounds like a driver hang mitigation kicking in. maybe kernel takes longer due to SM scheduler changes in 535+ drivers.

alice (ml-eng): i can repro locally on an A100 in our dev pool. curious: does this happen on Dedicated hosts (older driver)?

ben (infra): Dedicated hosts are on driver 525.x. can we test on one? if it's driver regression we can pin for now.

dmitri (ml-runtime): tested on a dedicated host (525.85) — no regressions, p95 ~115ms. so 535+ looks suspect. opening bug to NVIDIA but need a short-term mitigation.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4827: "CUDA14 driver regression: kernel launch timeouts causing Triton fallback for FP8 fused kernels" assigned to ben. :ticket:

ben (infra): assigned. mitigation ideas: 1) pin driver for Dedicated customers, 2) in Triton wrapper add a fast-path feature flag to prefer fused kernels via explicit envs, 3) add runtime metric to detect kernel fallthrough and auto-fallback to vLLM/trtllm alternate.

eva (research): for model onboarding, this explains why some GPTQ runs had higher quality deltas: the fallback path uses a different attention implementation which changes numerics slightly -> impacts evals at edge. we should mark those runs as "runtime-inconsistent" in the eval dashboard.

alice (ml-eng): good call — QA noticed small perplexity delta on one GPTQ config last week, couldn't reproduce — that was probably this. can we add model-level metadata when running bakeoffs capturing runtime kernel path and driver version?

dmitri (ml-runtime): yep, i can add a header to the bakeoff harness with fields: kernel_selector, driver_version, triton_version, allocator (dlmalloc/ptmalloc/onednn-algo). will push in a PR.

carla (sre): also add a quick smoke that runs 10 short inferences to detect kernel fallthrough early and mark the build as flaky. saves time.

ben (infra): for the immediate prod mitigation i'm going to roll out a Triton wrapper env var that forces fused kernels for FP8 models on CUDA14 hosts. fallback route: route requests to vLLM path if kernel fallback count > 5/min.

eva (research): can the eval dashboards correlate accuracy regressions to kernel fallthrough logs? if so we can retroactively re-label questionable evals.

dmitri (ml-runtime): yes — we'll emit a per-request tag `runtime.kernel_variant=fast|fallback` to traces. hooking that into the eval pipeline is straightforward.

alice (ml-eng): action items summary: dmitri -> PR with bakeoff metadata + trace tag; ben -> deploy Triton env wrapper + pin drivers for affected pools; carla -> add smoke test; eva -> run a re-eval for the 3 suspicious GPTQ runs and flag deltas.

ben (infra): timeline: wrapper + pinning rollout within 24hrs. i'll post status here. :rocket:

dmitri (ml-runtime): thanks. saving the logs and attaching to the INFRA ticket. if anyone finds a repro with AWQ where it also falls back please ping — that would change priority.

alice (ml-eng): noted. good catch team. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INFRA-4827 status updated -> in_progress (ben).
